newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EIB TO BOOST EUROPEAN FILM MAKING.
newsitem.headline: EIB TO BOOST EUROPEAN FILM MAKING.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) said on Wednesday it was lending 71 million European curency units ($92 million) to PolyGram NV to help it make European films. ING will underwrite the project.
"This is the first time the EIB has financed the film industry," EIB president Sir Brian Unwin said in a statement.

"We are doing so because the entertainment industry in Europe is making a growing contribution to the European Union's economy and is an important job creator," he said. "Our purpose is to enhance its international competitiveness.
The EIB said the money would be used by PolyGram to shoot films predominantly within the EU aimed at a family audience.
